claim: Evoked dopamine secretion is fast and relies on active zone-like release sites.
source: We recently found that evoked dopamine secretion is fast and relies on active zone-like release sites.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from recent work by the authors.

claim: Only a small percentage of dopamine varicosities are directly apposed to postsynaptic specializations.
source: In the striatum, dopamine is thought to act as a volume transmitter because only a small percentage of dopamine varicosities are directly apposed to postsynaptic specializations (Descarries et al., 1996; Wildenberg et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Descarries et al., 1996 and Wildenberg et al., 2021.

claim: Dopamine receptors are found mostly extrasynaptically.
source: dopamine receptors are found mostly extrasynaptically (Liu et al., 2021a; Rice et al., 2011; Sesack et al., 1994; Uchigashima et al., 2016; Yung et al., 1995)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Dopamine likely signals by diffusing through the extracellular striatal space before initiating responses in target cells.
source: Hence, dopamine likely signals by diffusing through the extracellular striatal space before initiating responses in target cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited evidence about dopamine varicosities and receptor localization.

claim: Dopamine release is rapid, has a high release probability, and occurs at small hotspots.
source: First, dopamine release is rapid, has a high release probability, and occurs at small hotspots (Banerjee et al., 2022; Banerjee et al., 2020; Beyene et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2018; Marcott et al., 2014; Patriarchi et al., 2018; Silm et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2014; Zych and Ford, 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: At least some dopamine receptors respond rapidly to local, high concentrations of dopamine.
source: Second, at least some dopamine receptors respond rapidly to local, high concentrations of dopamine (Beckstead et al., 2004; Condon et al., 2021; Courtney and Ford, 2014; Gantz et al., 2013; Marcott et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Dopamine neuron activity and secretion often correlate with behavior on fast time scales.
source: Third, dopamine neuron activity and secretion often correlate with behavior on fast time scales (Bova et al., 2020; Chaudhury et al., 2013; da Silva et al., 2018; Hamilos et al., 2021; Hollerman and Schultz, 1998; Howe and Dombeck, 2016; Jin and Costa, 2010; Schultz et al., 1997)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: RIM and Liprin-α are important for evoked dopamine release.
source: These proteins include the active zone scaffolds RIM and Liprin-α, the priming protein Munc13, and the fast Ca2+ sensor Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt-1) (Banerjee et al., 2022; Banerjee et al., 2020; Lebowitz et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018; Robinson et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Munc13 is important for evoked dopamine release.
source: These proteins include the active zone scaffolds RIM and Liprin-α, the priming protein Munc13, and the fast Ca2+ sensor Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt-1) (Banerjee et al., 2022; Banerjee et al., 2020; Lebowitz et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018; Robinson et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Synaptotagmin-1 is important for evoked dopamine release.
source: These proteins include the active zone scaffolds RIM and Liprin-α, the priming protein Munc13, and the fast Ca2+ sensor Synaptotagmin-1 (Syt-1) (Banerjee et al., 2022; Banerjee et al., 2020; Lebowitz et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018; Robinson et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: RIM-BP is dispensable for axonal dopamine release.
source: Conversely, the active zone scaffolds RIM-BP and ELKS are dispensable for axonal dopamine release, even though at least ELKS is present at these sites (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: ELKS is dispensable for axonal dopamine release.
source: Conversely, the active zone scaffolds RIM-BP and ELKS are dispensable for axonal dopamine release, even though at least ELKS is present at these sites (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: ELKS is present at dopamine release sites.
source: Conversely, the active zone scaffolds RIM-BP and ELKS are dispensable for axonal dopamine release, even though at least ELKS is present at these sites (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: Striatal dopamine release only partially depends on voltage-gated Ca2+ channels of the CaV2 family.
source: Striatal dopamine release only partially depends on voltage-gated Ca2+ channels of the CaV2 family, channels that are required for stimulated release at most synapses (Brimblecombe et al., 2015; Held et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022; Luebke et al., 1993; Takahashi and Momiyama, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: CaV2 family Ca2+ channels are required for stimulated release at most synapses.
source: Striatal dopamine release only partially depends on voltage-gated Ca2+ channels of the CaV2 family, channels that are required for stimulated release at most synapses (Brimblecombe et al., 2015; Held et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022; Luebke et al., 1993; Takahashi and Momiyama, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: 527 proteins were present at dopamine release sites when applying a threshold of ≥2.0-fold enrichment over soluble axonal proteins.
source: Using three different release site bait proteins, we found that 527 proteins were present at these sites when we applied a threshold of ≥2.0-fold enrichment over soluble axonal proteins.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: 190 proteins were enriched in multiple bait conditions.
source: A total of 190 proteins were enriched in multiple bait conditions and 41 proteins with all three baits.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: 41 proteins were enriched with all three baits.
source: A total of 190 proteins were enriched in multiple bait conditions and 41 proteins with all three baits.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: α-Synuclein was enriched at dopamine release sites.
source: α-Synuclein, a protein linked to Parkinson's disease, was enriched at release sites, and its enrichment was lost in both tested mutants.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: α-Synuclein enrichment was lost in RIM knockout mice.
source: α-Synuclein, a protein linked to Parkinson's disease, was enriched at release sites, and its enrichment was lost in both tested mutants.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data comparing control and mutant mice.

claim: α-Synuclein enrichment was lost in Synaptotagmin-1 knockout mice.
source: α-Synuclein, a protein linked to Parkinson's disease, was enriched at release sites, and its enrichment was lost in both tested mutants.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data comparing control and mutant mice.

claim: RIM organizes scaffolded dopamine release sites.
source: We conclude that RIM organizes scaffolded dopamine release sites and provide a proteomic assessment of the composition of these sites.

claim: For RIMPPCP-BirA and ELKS2β-BirA, 50% and 54% of the detected proteins were higher than with BirA-tdTomato.
source: For RIMPPCP-BirA (Figure 1D) and ELKS2β-BirA (Figure 1E), 50% and 54% of the detected proteins were higher than with BirA-tdTomato, and 20% and 25% were above the 2.0-fold enrichment threshold, respectively.

claim: For RIMPPCP-BirA and ELKS2β-BirA, 20% and 25% were above the 2.0-fold enrichment threshold.
source: For RIMPPCP-BirA (Figure 1D) and ELKS2β-BirA (Figure 1E), 50% and 54% of the detected proteins were higher than with BirA-tdTomato, and 20% and 25% were above the 2.0-fold enrichment threshold, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct quantification from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: Only 30% of all proteins detected in the CaVβ4-BirA condition were higher compared to BirA-tdTomato.
source: Only 30% of all proteins detected in the CaVβ4-BirA condition were higher compared to BirA-tdTomato, and 9% were enriched ≥2.0-fold.

claim: 9% of proteins detected in the CaVβ4-BirA condition were enriched ≥2.0-fold.
source: Only 30% of all proteins detected in the CaVβ4-BirA condition were higher compared to BirA-tdTomato, and 9% were enriched ≥2.0-fold.

claim: Ca2+ entry in dopamine axons is widespread.
source: They are also consistent with functional analyses that revealed that Ca2+ entry in dopamine axons is widespread (Pereira et al., 2016)

claim: Of the 527 enriched proteins, 194 (37%) have one or multiple synaptic cellular compartment annotations in SynGO.
source: Of the 527 enriched proteins, 194 (37%) have one or multiple synaptic cellular compartment annotations in SynGO (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the study's data using the SynGO database.

claim: 102 proteins (19% of the entire dataset, 53% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) have a presynaptic annotation.
source: A total of 102 proteins (19% of the entire dataset, 53% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) have a presynaptic annotation with many having additional specific assignments to the active zone or synaptic vesicles
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the study's data using the SynGO database.

claim: 87 proteins (17% of the entire dataset, 45% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) have postsynaptic annotations.
source: while 87 (17% of the entire dataset, 45% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) have postsynaptic annotations (Figure 2B).

claim: 43 proteins (8% of the entire dataset, 22% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) are annotated both pre- and postsynaptically.
source: Also, 43 proteins (8% of the entire dataset, 22% of the SynGO synaptic proteins) are annotated both pre- and postsynaptically.
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the study's data using the SynGO database.

claim: RIM1 (Rims1), ELKS2 (Erc2), and Bassoon (Bsn) were all enriched across multiple conditions.
source: Indeed, RIM1 (Rims1), ELKS2 (Erc2), and Bassoon (Bsn), proteins that can be used as markers for dopamine release sites (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018) and that were shown to be associated with synaptic vesicle docking sites using a different proteomic approach (Boyken et al., 2013), were all enriched across multiple conditions (Figure 2A).

source: Of the 527 enriched proteins with the ≥2.0-fold threshold, 333 (63%) do not have a SynGO annotation (Figure 2B)

claim: Neuroplastin is strongly enriched across conditions.
source: Neuroplastin is strongly enriched across conditions (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: In TH-positive particles, Neuroplastin antibody staining intensity was significantly higher when Bassoon was present.
source: In particles labeled with TH, Neuroplastin antibody staining intensity was significantly higher when Bassoon was present (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).

claim: In RIM cKODA mice, 31% (RIMPPCP-BirA), 12% (ELKS2β-BirA), and 13% (CaVβ4-BirA) of the identified proteins were higher than with BirA-tdTomato.
source: In RIM cKODA mice, 31% (RIMPPCP-BirA), 12% (ELKS2β-BirA), and 13% (CaVβ4-BirA) of the identified proteins were higher than with BirA-tdTomato
evidence: This is a direct quantification from the study's mass spectrometry data in RIM knockout mice.

claim: In RIM cKODA mice, 14% (RIMPPCP-BirA), 6% (ELKS2β-BirA), and 4% (CaVβ4-BirA) reached the ≥2.0-fold enrichment threshold.
source: and 14% (RIMPPCP-BirA), 6% (ELKS2β-BirA), and 4% (CaVβ4-BirA) reached the ≥2.0-fold enrichment threshold to be considered hits (Figure 3C–E).

claim: In Syt-1 cKODA mice, protein enrichment over BirA-tdTomato was more similar to the control proteome.

claim: The RIM cKODA dataset contained a total of 198 hits.
source: The RIM cKODA dataset contained a total of 198 hits (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), compared to the 527 hits in the control proteome (Figure 2).

claim: Expression of RIMPPCP may restore some scaffolding deficits caused by RIM cKODA.

claim: In Syt-1 cKODA mice, 450 hits were detected with the 2.0-fold enrichment threshold.

source: In contrast, 37% of the proteins in the control dataset were also enriched in the Syt-1 cKODA dataset (Figure 4E).

source: Our control dataset contained five of these genes: Snca, Park7, Dnajc6, Synj-1, and Vps35 (Figure 6A).

claim: Snca was ≥2.0-fold enriched in each condition.

claim: In both RIM cKODA and Syt-1 cKODA mice, α-synuclein enrichment was reduced and fell below the 2.0-fold threshold.
source: In both RIM cKODA and Syt-1 cKODA mice, α-synuclein enrichment was reduced and fell below the 2.0-fold threshold (Figure 6B, Figure 3—figure supplements 1A and 2A).

claim: α-Synuclein is associated with synaptic vesicles and regulates synaptic vesicle clustering, SNARE complex formation, and endocytosis.
source: α-Synuclein is associated with synaptic vesicles and regulates synaptic vesicle clustering, SNARE complex formation, and endocytosis (Burré et al., 2010; Diao et al., 2013; Murphy et al., 2000).

source: RIM or Syt-1 knockout causes a loss of docked vesicles at synapses (Chang et al., 2018; Kaeser et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: Mutations in RIMS genes increase the risk of Parkinson's disease and are key drivers of disease progression.
source: Loss of dopamine neurons underlies the motor symptoms characteristic of Parkinson's disease (Poewe et al., 2017), and recent human genetic studies establish that mutations in RIMS genes increase the risk of Parkinson's disease and are key drivers of disease progression (Liu et al., 2021b; Nalls et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human genetic studies.

claim: Dopamine neurons corelease glutamate and GABA.

claim: GABA is loaded into vesicles via VMAT2.
source: While GABA is loaded into vesicles via VMAT2 (Melani and Tritsch, 2022; Tritsch et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

source: Second, dopamine axons receive input from cholinergic interneurons (Cachope et al., 2012; Threlfell et al., 2012; Zhou et al., 2001)

claim: Activation of nicotinic receptors triggers dopamine axon action potential firing.

Striatal dopamine axons make sparse synaptic-like connections with medium spiny neurons that contain the GABAergic postsynaptic scaffold Gephyrin (Uchigashima et al., 2016; Wildenberg et al., 2021).

source: Gephyrin (Gphn) was indeed enriched with ELKS2β-BirA and RIMPPCP-BirA (Figure 2).

source: It is noteworthy that in our experiments dopamine receptors were not enriched, consistent with their localization outside of the postsynaptic scaffolds in target neurons (Uchigashima et al., 2016).

claim: The estimated labeling radius of iBioID is up to 50 nm.

source: Peptides from 1969 proteins were identified in at least one of the BirA conditions.

source: A total of 300 (15%) of those proteins are mitochondrial proteins, which is common in iBioID, and these proteins were removed from further analyses unless noted otherwise, as has been done before (Loh et al., 2016; Uezu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: RIM ablation does not severely disrupt release site structure at classical synapses when assessed with microscopy.
source: Although similar proteomic approaches were not performed, RIM ablation does not severely disrupt release site structure at classical synapses when assessed with microscopy, but redundant scaffolds might maintain the sites instead (Acuna et al., 2016; de Jong et al., 2018; Emperador-Melero and Kaeser, 2020; Kaeser et al., 2011; Kushibiki et al., 2019; Oh et al., 2021; Tan et al., 2022a; Tan et al., 2022b; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Dopamine release site scaffolding may have less redundancy and rely heavily on RIM.
source: Overall, our work supports the model that dopamine release site scaffolding may have less redundancy and rely heavily on RIM (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: The BirA fusion proteins were detected within TH-labeled axons.
source: The fusion proteins were detected within TH-labeled axons.

claim: RIMPPCP-BirA and ELKS2β-BirA were present in small punctate structures consistent with release site localization.
source: RIMPPCP-BirA and ELKS2β-BirA were present in small punctate structures consistent with release site localization (Liu et al., 2018).

claim: CaVβ4 appeared somewhat more widespread, similar to Ca2+ entry in these axons.
source: CaVβ4 appeared somewhat more widespread, similar to Ca2+ entry in these axons (Pereira et al., 2016)

claim: BirA-tdTomato was broadly overlapping with TH, likely reflecting a soluble axonal localization.
source: and BirA-tdTomato was broadly overlapping with TH, likely reflecting a soluble axonal localization.

claim: In vivo biotinylation was confirmed for the BirA fusion proteins with or without biotin injections.
source: In vivo biotinylation was next confirmed for the BirA fusion proteins with or without biotin injections (for 7 days) followed by pilot biotin-affinity purifications and Western blotting of the purified fractions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is based on Western blot experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Biotinylation and protein purification are efficient.
source: This established that biotinylation and protein purification are efficient, and that background biotinylation in the absence of biotin is limited.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Western blot experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Background biotinylation in the absence of biotin is limited.
source: This established that biotinylation and protein purification are efficient, and that background biotinylation in the absence of biotin is limited.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Western blot experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Four independent biological repeats per BirA fusion protein were performed.
source: In total, four independent biological repeats per BirA fusion protein were performed (i.e., four times 10–12 striata per condition, conditions: RIMPPCP-BirA, ELKS2β-BirA, CaVβ4-BirA, BirA-tdTomato, also see 'Materials and methods').

claim: The four repeats were run as two large experiments for in vivo biotinylation, biotin affinity purification, and mass spectrometry.
source: The four repeats were run as two large experiments for in vivo biotinylation, biotin affinity purification, and mass spectrometry; two repeats were run in parallel in each experiment, and the two experiments were run approximately 1 year apart from one another
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The protein that was used as a bait was robustly enriched in each condition.
source: In each condition, the protein that was used as a BirA bait was robustly enriched (individually labeled proteins in Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Self-biotinylation of the BirA fusion proteins should be high compared to other proteins if the labeling radius is small.
source: This further establishes the approach, as self-biotinylation of the BirA fusion proteins should be high compared to other proteins if the labeling radius is small, which has been estimated to be 10–50 nm (Kim et al., 2014; Roux et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data and supported by citations about the labeling radius.

claim: The labeling radius of BirA has been estimated to be 10–50 nm.
source: This further establishes the approach, as self-biotinylation of the BirA fusion proteins should be high compared to other proteins if the labeling radius is small, which has been estimated to be 10–50 nm (Kim et al., 2014; Roux et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: Changing enrichment thresholds did not increase the percentage of synaptic proteins as identified via SynGO.
source: Changing enrichment thresholds did not increase the percentage of synaptic proteins as identified via SynGO (31% for ≥1.5 and 33% for ≥2.5 thresholds, respectively, Figure 2—figure supplement 3), justifying the use of ≥2.0 as the threshold for further analyses.
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the study's data with different thresholds.

claim: The number of proteins and peptide counts were similar across control, RIM cKODA, and Syt-1 cKODA experiments in the BirA-tdTomato condition.

claim: Removal of RIM or Syt-1 from dopamine neurons did not cause strong disruptions in the overall dopamine axon protein content in the striatum.
source: Hence, removal of RIM or Syt-1 from dopamine neurons did not cause strong disruptions in the overall dopamine axon protein content in the striatum.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of BirA-tdTomato data across genotypes.

claim: TH axon density is similar to control mice in RIM cKODA and Syt-1 cKODA mutants.

claim: RIM removal disrupts mechanisms important for release site scaffolding.
source: This suggests that RIM removal disrupts mechanisms important for release site scaffolding.

source: Abolishing synchronous dopamine release by Syt-1 cKODA has no strong effects on the overall number of proteins detected at release sites in dopamine axons with iBioID.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the enrichment data between control and Syt-1 knockout mice.

claim: RIM1 enrichment was absent from all conditions except for RIMPPCP-BirA in RIM cKODA mice.
source: RIM1 enrichment was absent from all conditions except for RIMPPCP-BirA, which likely reflects self-biotinylation of the bait.
evidence: This is a direct result from the mass spectrometry data in RIM knockout mice.

claim: In the control dataset, synaptic proteins were enriched.
source: In the control dataset (gray bars), synaptic proteins were enriched as expected (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is a direct result from analyzing the control data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The extent of enrichment had a tendency to increase as the SynGO annotation became more specific (to presynaptic and to active zone).
source: and the extent of enrichment had a tendency to increase as the SynGO annotation became more specific (to presynaptic, Figure 4B, and to active zone, Figure 4C).

claim: For ELKS2β-BirA and CaVβ4-BirA in RIM cKODA mice, proteins in all three SynGO categories appeared depleted.

claim: The depletion is absent in the RIMPPCP-BirA condition in RIM cKODA mice, supporting that release site scaffolding is partially restored.
source: The depletion is absent in the RIMPPCP-BirA condition in RIM cKODA mice, supporting that release site scaffolding is partially restored.

claim: The proteins found in the Syt-1 cKODA dataset show an enrichment that is overall relatively similar to the control dataset.
source: In contrast to RIM cKODA, the proteins found in the Syt-1 cKODA dataset show an enrichment that is overall relatively similar to the control dataset with all conditions having log2 fold change values >0 (Figure 4A–C, maroon bars)

claim: Twenty-two proteins were enriched with all three baits in RIM cKODA mice.
source: Twenty-two proteins were enriched with all three baits in RIM cKODA mice, indicating overlapping labeling radii with a resulting proteome relying on bait colocalization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct result from the mass spectrometry data in RIM knockout mice.

claim: Overall dopamine axon morphology was not strongly disrupted in RIM cKODA mice apart from changes in Bassoon clustering.
source: In a previous study, overall dopamine axon morphology was not strongly disrupted in RIM cKODA mice apart from changes in Bassoon clustering (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The general axonal proteome identified by BirA-tdTomato was similar between RIM cKODA and control mice.
source: Here, the general axonal proteome identified by BirA-tdTomato was similar between RIM cKODA and control mice (Figure 3B), arguing for a generally intact axonal arbor in these mice.
evidence: This is a direct result from comparing the BirA-tdTomato data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There is good overlap between the axonal proteins identified with BirA-tdTomato in our experiments with those in Hobson et al., 2022.
source: Indeed, there is good overlap between the axonal proteins identified with BirA-tdTomato in our experiments with those in Hobson et al., 2022, with 65% of the proteins identified here also present with the APEX2-based method.
evidence: This is a comparison with a previous study using a different method.

claim: RIM1 (Rims1), Bassoon (Bsn), ELKS1 (Erc1), ELKS2 (Erc2), P/Q-type (CaV2.1, Cacna1a) and N-type Ca2+ channels (CaV2.2, Cacna1b) were all detected.
source: RIM1 (Rims1), Bassoon (Bsn), and ELKS1 (Erc1), ELKS2 (Erc2), and P/Q-type (CaV2.1, Cacna1a) and N-type Ca2+ channels (CaV2.2, Cacna1b) were all detected, consistent with previous studies that assessed roles and/or localization of these proteins in dopamine neurons (Banerjee et al., 2022; Brimblecombe et al., 2015; Daniel et al., 2009; Ducrot et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018; Uchigashima et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: Liprin-α2 and -α3 knockout has less severe effects on dopamine release compared to RIM knockout.
source: We found that Liprin-α2 and -α3 knockout has less severe effects on dopamine release compared to RIM knockout, while removal of RIM-BP leaves dopamine release unimpaired (Banerjee et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Striatal dopamine release is strongly impaired after Munc13 ablation.
source: Striatal dopamine release is strongly impaired after Munc13 ablation (Banerjee et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Munc13 was only enriched in some cases with iBioID.
source: but only enriched in some cases with iBioID (Figures 2 and 5, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: At synapses, some Munc13 may be more broadly distributed than just at active zones.
source: At synapses, some Munc13 may be more broadly distributed than just at active zones (Tan et al., 2022a; Tan et al., 2022b)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations.

claim: Munc13 was also absent in the release site proteome assessed via docked vesicles.
source: Notably, Munc13 was also absent in the release site proteome assessed via docked vesicles (Boyken et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous proteomic study.

claim: Biotinylation across membranes may be common in iBioID.
source: Biotinylation across membranes may be common in iBioID, and detection of intramitochondrial proteins and of synaptic vesicle proteins with postsynaptic baits has been observed (Uezu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Cend1 appears both in our data and a previous vesicle docking proteome.
source: Cend1, for example, a protein associated with cell cycle exit, appears both in our data and a previous vesicle docking proteome, and electron microscopic studies suggested that it might be present at the presynaptic plasma membrane (Boyken et al., 2013; Patsavoudi et al., 1995; Politis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison with a previous study and is supported by citations.

claim: Hist1h1d and Hist1h4a, genes encoding for the histone proteins H1.3 and H4, were robustly enriched.
source: It is surprising that Hist1h1d and Hist1h4a, genes encoding for the histone proteins H1.3 and H4, were robustly enriched (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Several kinesins (Kif21a, Kif21b, Kif5a, Kif5b) were enriched.
source: Indeed, several kinesins (Kif21a, Kif21b, Kif5a, Kif5b) were enriched, possibly reflecting transport packets.
evidence: This is a direct result from the study's mass spectrometry data.

claim: The synaptic ribosomes that reached the 2.0-fold threshold across conditions may reflect hits by non-active zone-localized bait proteins.
source: The synaptic ribosomes (Figure 5) that reached the 2.0-fold threshold across conditions may also reflect hits by non-active zone-localized bait proteins.
evidence: This is speculation about the interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Before PC depletion, 28% and 10% of the detected peptides were from PC and the related protein propionyl-CoA carboxylase (PCCA), respectively.
source: In pilot experiments, we assessed the efficiency of PC depletion. Before PC depletion, 28% and 10% of the detected peptides were from PC and the related protein propionyl-CoA carboxylase (PCCA), respectively.
evidence: This is a direct result from pilot experiments.

claim: After PC depletion, 3% and 1.7% of the detected peptides were from PC and PCCA, respectively.
source: After depletion, 3% and 1.7% of the detected peptides were from PC and PCCA, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct result from pilot experiments.
